A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DASH diet, rich in fruits and vegetables, low-fat dairy products and reduced in saturated and total fat, reduces blood pressure and is a healthy dietary pattern for all Americans.
the DASH dietary pattern is effective for lowering blood pressure in both hypertensive and nonhypertensive individuals.
a DASH diet with a low sodium intake (1500mg) is more effective than a low sodium intake alone (2400mg) in lowering blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low-salt diet is not harmful and may be beneficial.
reducing sodium intake, especially to levels that are much lower than current intake, will lower blood pressure in the majority of people, regardless of whether they have hypertension or not.

a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat or non-fat dairy products, and low in saturated and total fat, cholesterol, refined grains, sweets, and sodium, is the most important dietary change that individuals with hypertension can make to improve their blood pressure and reduce their risk for cardiovascular disease.
